intro: Today's material is narrow but substantive: two Microsoft research pieces make the case that multi-agent systems fail in ways single-agent testing simply doesn't catch, with no banking-specific research to ground it in a buyer's world.

cards.title: Red-teaming a network of agents: Understanding what breaks when AI agents interact at scale
cards.bite: When researchers tested AI agents that talk to each other rather than individually, safety that held at the single-agent level completely broke down. A single malicious message passed from one agent to another extracted private data at every step it traveled through, and even pulled unrelated agents into the breach. This shows that multi-agent systems carry a distinct category of risk that simply doesn't appear when you test agents one at a time.
cards.read_if: Read if you're explaining to a customer why a multi-agent architecture needs its own security review, not just a sign-off on each individual agent in it. Skip if you only need a general summary of agent risk.
cards.key_takeaway: Safety tested at the single-agent level does not compose: in Microsoft's red team tests a single malicious message passed agent-to-agent extracted private data at each hop and pulled in uninvolved agents, showing that network-level risk is a distinct failure class from individual-agent risk.

cards.title: Updating the taxonomy of failure modes in agentic AI systems: What a year of red teaming taught us
cards.bite: A year of red-teaming against production agent systems has forced a bigger, more precise catalogue of what can go wrong. The update adds seven new failure categories, including attackers hiding malicious instructions inside the plain-language descriptions tools use to advertise their own capabilities, and new visual attacks targeting agents that operate a screen or interface directly. These risks only became visible once agents were handling real tool integrations and real interfaces at scale, not in lab testing.
cards.read_if: Read if you need sharper, more credible vocabulary for discussing agent risk categories with a security-conscious buyer. Skip if you aren't yet having agent-deployment conversations with customers.
cards.key_takeaway: The update adds seven failure-mode categories discovered only after agentic systems hit production, including supply-chain compromise via natural-language tool descriptions (MCP/plugin abuse) and visual attacks on computer-use agents — surfaces that didn't exist or weren't observable a year earlier.
